items.title: Dominance from a scheme with finitely many irreducible components is detected on generic points of the irreducible components of the target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that when X has finitely many irreducible components, dominance of f : X to S is equivalent to every irreducible component of S having its generic point in the image of f, and that S then has finitely many irreducible components as well (statement lines 1382-1390). The proof is a short but genuine topological argument: it decomposes X into components Z_i with generic points xi_i, uses that the image of an irreducible set is irreducible and that closure commutes with finite unions to obtain the display S = union of the closures of {f(xi_i)}, and then reads both conclusions off that display (proof lines 1392-1404). It is H2: the input is the generic-point dictionary for irreducible components, but the union-of-closures manipulation and the passage from generic points in the image to the statement about components are carried out inside the counted span.
